summary: Iteration 4: verified gallery MongoDB CRUD + WhatsApp floating button features. Backend: 7/7 new pytest cases passed (public GET /api/gallery returns 16 sorted visible photos with no _id; admin CRUD create/update/delete with proper auth; 401 no-token; 403 viewer; 404 on unknown id; whatsapp field in Settings model and persists via PUT /api/admin/settings). Frontend: /galeri masonry renders 16 photos, lightbox open/next/prev/close works. WhatsApp button correctly hidden when settings.whatsapp='', appears with correct href=https://wa.me/905001234567 and target=_blank on public pages (/, /menu, /rezervasyon), NOT rendered on /admin. Admin flow with session cookie: Galeri tab shows 16 cards; uploading /app/frontend/public/images/latte.jpg via gallery-upload-btn creates a 17th card AND appears on public /galeri (17); toggling gallery-toggle-{id} hides it from public GET (back to 16 public, still 17 admin); gallery-delete-{id} with confirm dialog removes it (back to 16 admin). Ayarlar tab: settings-whatsapp-input persists the saved value. No webpack-dev-server overlay observed. No pageerrors. Cleanup performed: whatsapp reset to '', uploaded test photo deleted, gallery back to 16.

issues: Reservation form uses browser-native date (mm/dd/yyyy) and time (--:--) inputs instead of a locale-aware/shadcn date picker — Turkish site users would expect dd/mm/yyyy or a custom picker. Pre-existing, not introduced by this iteration.

critical_code_review_comments: GalleryPhoto model + endpoints are clean (_id excluded, sorted by order, visible filter on public). CRUD auth via require_admin properly returns 401/403.
WhatsAppButton correctly strips non-digits from settings.whatsapp before building wa.me URL and hides itself on /admin routes and when the value is empty.
AdminGallery upload flow chains /admin/upload -> /admin/gallery cleanly; alt defaults to filename sans extension, order auto-set to photos.length — reasonable.
Minor: PUT /api/admin/gallery/{id} returns {ok:true} instead of the updated document; UI reloads via full GET which is fine, but returning the updated object would save a round trip.
